title: I tied a rope at the cave entrance to find my way out. Something tugged it.
transcript:
I tied a rope at the cave entrance to find my way out. Something tugged it. The rope in my hand went tight, then tugged. Twice. Like someone at the entrance wanted my attention.

Nobody knew I was down there. I'd tied my yellow rope to the iron ring at the cave mouth and fed it out behind me the whole way in. Follow it back, and you can't get lost. A minute ago I'd set it down to fix my headlamp. My lamp had maybe an hour left.

Two more tugs. Harder.

Then a voice, far up the tunnel. "Hello? Are you hurt?" A ranger, I thought. I almost cried. "Follow the rope," he called. "I've got you."

So I did. Hand over hand through the dark, the rope pulling a little with every step, helping me along.

My lamp flickered. The tunnel got narrower. Colder. I didn't remember squeezing through here on the way in.

"Almost there," the voice said. Closer now. And lower. Somewhere below me.

I pointed my lamp at my hands. The rope wasn't yellow. It was black, and slick, and it was moving on its own.

Then it started reeling me in.
